title: Cold rebuild: Parse a tcpdump line
summary: Rebuild Parse a tcpdump line from memory, no hints.

steps.title: Cold rebuild
body: Time to prove a piece stuck. You built **Parse a tcpdump line** in *Packet capture*. Now write it again from an
**empty editor**: no starter, no hints, no solution to peek at. The tests are exactly the ones you passed
Why: pulling something out of memory is what makes it stay there. Reading your old code feels like knowing
it; rebuilding it cold shows whether you do. If you get stuck, that is useful news: go back to the lesson,
then come back and try again tomorrow.
This check, plus the boss, is what proves the module.

steps.prompt: A capture shows `[S]` from the client to port 5432, then immediately `[R.]` back. What do you conclude?
options: The host is up but nothing listens on 5432
steps.explain: A reset is an active answer: the host's kernel saying no. A firewall drop would show `[S]` repeated with no reply.

steps.title: Rebuild Parse a tcpdump line cold
prompt: Write `(string SrcIp, int SrcPort, string DstIp, int DstPort, string Flags) ParseLine(string line)` for lines like
The port is after the **last** dot of each address; the destination ends with `:`. `Flags` is the text inside the brackets (`S`, `S.`, `R.`).
**From memory this time:** the editor starts empty and the tests are the ones you passed in the lesson.
Type the shape yourself, then fill it in:
(string SrcIp, int SrcPort, string DstIp, int DstPort, string Flags) ParseLine(string line)
